headline: A Schwab strategist warns that one large company cutting its AI spending could unsettle a market that AI stocks now carry.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a strategist's warning on market concentration, not a market event.
importance_line: People who own index funds are indirectly exposed to a few large AI spenders, and the warning is one strategist's view, tied to the coming earnings season.
summary: BeInCrypto reports, as carried by Yahoo Finance, that Charles Schwab's head of macro research and strategy Kevin Gordon told Bloomberg This Weekend that a single miss in AI spending by one very large company could start to disrupt earnings. He noted the S&P 500 sits about 1% below its high while the average member stock has had a 14% peak-to-trough drop since early August.
notes: Yahoo Finance carries a BeInCrypto article by Darryn Pollock (named in the article), which relays Gordon's remarks on Bloomberg This Weekend; source credited to BeInCrypto citing Bloomberg, not Yahoo. The 14% figure is the average drop of members since early August, not their loss today. Third-quarter earnings season opens this month.
